title: Security of Quantum Conference Key Agreement with Two-Way Classical Communication
authors: Shun Kawakami, Mori Watanabe, Takuya Ikuta, Koichi Takasugi
abstract: Quantum conference key agreement (QCKA) enables multiple users to establish a common secret key with information-theoretic security and is regarded as a key primitive for secure communication in future quantum networks. However, practical implementations of QCKA typically suffer from higher noise levels than conventional bipartite quantum key distribution (QKD), making the improvement of the tolerable error threshold an important challenge. Gottesman and Lo proposed two preprocessing procedures for QKD with two-way classical communication, known as the B-step and the P-step, which enhance the tolerable error threshold. In this paper, we analyze the asymptotic security of QCKA with tripartite GHZ states and two measurement bases using two-way classical communication, including multiple B-steps and P-steps. We derive the corresponding secure key rate analytically and demonstrate that iterative B-steps can increase the tolerable error threshold beyond 20%, significantly improving upon the approximately 11% threshold achievable without two-way classical communication and the approximately 15% threshold obtained with only a single B-step. Our results show that two-way classical communication can substantially enhance the robustness of practical QCKA protocols.
summary: This paper analyzes the security of Quantum Conference Key Agreement using GHZ states, focusing on enhancing its resilience against noise. By incorporating multiple two-way classical communication steps (B-steps and P-steps), the authors derive that the tolerable error threshold can be significantly increased. This demonstrates a major improvement in the practical feasibility of QCKA for future quantum networks.
main_problem: The primary challenge is improving the tolerable error threshold for Quantum Conference Key Agreement (QCKA) protocols, which are crucial for future quantum networks.
main_result: Iterative application of B-steps can significantly boost the tolerable error threshold beyond 20%, substantially enhancing the robustness of practical GHZ-based QCKA protocols.
method: The authors derive the asymptotic secure key rate by analytically analyzing the optimization problem associated with multiple B-steps and P-steps applied to the QCKA protocol.
model_or_system: The system models Quantum Conference Key Agreement (QCKA) among three users using tripartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, restricted to two complementary measurement bases (Z and X).
key_observables: Secure key rate ($R$) and the tolerable error threshold.
important_parameters: Error rates ($	ext{s}_1, 	ext{s}_2, 	ext{s}_3, 	ext{s}_4$), which are optimized subject to physical constraints derived from probability amplitudes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an Independent and Identically Distributed (IID) interaction for the eavesdropper Eve across rounds, and that only two measurement bases are used for practical relevance.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the security by defining the QCKA protocol using GHZ states. It then derives the key rate formula incorporating error correction steps (B-step, P-step) and solves the resulting optimization problem to maximize robustness against noise.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical limitations in quantum networking protocols by providing concrete methods (iterative B-steps) to enhance fault tolerance beyond current theoretical limits.
